name: Implicit BC
summary: Florence et al. replaced explicit action regression with an energy-based model that scores state-action pairs, selecting actions by optimization at inference. This addresses the core pathology of mean-squared-error behavior cloning: when expert behavior is multimodal, averaging the modes yields an action correct nowhere. Implicit BC solved precise contact-rich tasks that explicit policies failed outright.
innovation: Energy-based policy formulation making multimodal and discontinuous behavior representable.
Demonstrated the loss function, not capacity, was blocking precise manipulation.
matters: Framed the multimodality problem that Diffusion Policy would later solve more practically.
limits: Inference requires an optimization step over actions: slow and finicky to tune.
lineage: A direct critique and repair of the regression objective inherited from ALVINN-style cloning.
